setup: (fset 'my-when (if (fboundp 'defmacro) (cons 'macro (lambda (c b) (list 'if c b))) (macro (c b) (list 'if c b))))
note: 10B, the measured alias rule: one step follows exactly one `defalias` link and hands back the rewritten form, so a two-link chain answers the middle link `(ali 7)` rather than the transformer's result. This is why the implementation does not resolve the whole chain the way call position does. The setup is dialect-neutral by construction: Emacs stores a macro as a `(macro . FUNCTION)` cons in the function cell and fe has a distinct macro object, so each transformer is installed through whichever spelling the running dialect has, selected by `(fboundp 'defmacro)` -- t in Emacs, nil in standalone fe. Nothing else about the case differs between the sides. The transformers deliberately expand to forms both dialects spell identically (`if`, `+`, `not`): fe's implicit body is `do` where Emacs' is `progn`, and fe prints `(quote x)` where Emacs prints `'x`, and neither of those is what these cases are about.
